title: Authentication vs authorization
idea: Authentication proves who is calling. Authorization decides what that caller may do. A server asks the first question, then the second.

analogy.text: A members-only club. The door checks your ID to learn who you are. The staff then check the list for which rooms you may enter.
analogy.breaks: A club checks once at the door; a server checks every request.

points: Authentication checks a credential: a password, a session cookie or a token.
Authorization checks the caller's role, such as `user` or `admin`, or record ownership.
Authorization needs an identity, so it can only run after authentication succeeds.
No valid login gets `401`; a known user without permission gets `403`.

hero.title: Two checks, always in this order

steps.caption: `authenticate` looks for a login and finds none. It cannot say who is calling.
No identity means `401`. The request stops here and `authorize` never runs.
Request 2 comes from Ada, logged in with role `user`. `authenticate` knows who she is and passes her on.
`authorize` asks whether role `user` may delete a book. Only `admin` may.
Known but not allowed means `403`. The handler never runs.
Request 3 comes from Root, an admin. Both checks pass.
`204` means done, with no body to send back.

code.title: 401 first, then 403
code.caption: The `Map` lookup stands in for a verified login. Later pages build these checks as `authenticate` and `requireRole` middleware.

pitfalls: Do not send `403` when there is no login; that case is `401`.
Never trust a `role` sent in the body; read it from the verified login.
Hiding a button is not authorization. Check permission on the server for every request.

quiz.why: `ada` is known but not an admin, so `403`. `root` is an admin: `200`. `eve` is unknown, so `401` comes first.

takeaway: Knowing who someone is never tells you what they may do.

starters: Why is `401` called Unauthorized when it means unauthenticated?
Can a request be authorized without being authenticated?
Where in an Express app do these two checks live?
